summary: The image loader-diag-xnu-ckpt3-usb was built on the host from the committed NAT-036 resumable-checkpoint and NAT-047 USB-log patch pipelines plus a new glue (patch_ckpt52.py, src/glue52*.h): at each of the 22 arrivals of nat036_ckpt_c the stub installs the loader's vectors, queues one 'CK ...' text record (stop index, kernel state, esr/elr/far for an early exception), services the NAT-041 EP0 engine for 0.3 s and restores the kernel's vectors; the final hold announces itself with a HOLD record. In unicorn, against the NAT-041 DWC3 model and the unmodified s24_logd collector, all 22 notes arrive complete and in order through kernel gaps with no polling (up to 8 s), an early exception arrives with esr/elr/far, an engine that never came up leaves the kernel path unchanged, and the model chain's end state equals an uninterrupted run. 45 tests pass; the mutation check kills 14 of 15 mutants and documents 1 as equivalent. One RECOVERY candidate (hashes only) is packaged and a decision draft for one future run is written. Nothing ran on the phone and nothing was flashed.
evidence_category: host-test (patch/build checks, aarch64 instruction-level model chain, unicorn run of the built loader against NAT-041's DWC3 model and collector); not a measurement of the S24

The glue services the engine only from the loader's stub at nat036_ckpt_c (never from XNU), writes one record per arrival and one HOLD record. DEVIATION from the wording: the record carries the NAT-035 resume state (x2, x3, mask, sctlr, sp, kttbr0, vbar, and esr/elr/far for an early exception) and not SPSR/ELR of a return, because a resumable return is not an exception return; the boot id is the collector's BOOT record.

established: Source/host-test: the glue patches apply exactly once each, all-or-nothing, and only the intended hunks change; the build is reproducible, has no SIMD or misaligned access, and fits the 2 MiB block at each known S-Boot base.

Host-test: with the unmodified NAT-041 collector, the 22 notes of a run with kernel gaps without polling reach the archive complete, in order, with zero drops, and the earlier loader log precedes them.
Host-test: the loader's vectors are in place while the engine is serviced and the kernel's are back afterwards, also when the engine never came up.
not_established: Anything about the real S24: DWC3 behaviour after a stretch with no polling, cache coherence of the engine DMA block with the kernel's caches, the fixed 0.3 s service window, the time budget of real kernel gaps and draws, and the NAT-045 HSI0 sequence itself (first tested by NAT-043).
That a host sees any of it: the udev rule for 1209:0001 is not installed (NAT-050 blocked on the owner's root) and NAT-043 has not run.
The simulation has no caches, MMU, interrupts or real controller; the model is one reading of the databook and the vendor driver, and a shared misreading is invisible to the tests.
Kernel execution past C checkpoint 16; x0..x30 at an exception; SPSR of the stopped context.
findings: Mutant M10 (counter incremented only while the engine is up) is a documented equivalent: n->up is 0 until nat047_bringup, becomes 1 once, and can only go back to 0 on a poll fault; notes are written only while it is 1.

The first mutation run (artifacts/nat-052/mutants-001.log) found two things: g_nat052_depth was written but never read (removed; the image changed, build-003 supersedes build-001/002), and nothing checked that setups= is a delta since the previous note (test added: test_setups_is_what_the_engine_served_since_the_previous_note_not_a_running_total). The 15-mutant run recorded here is the rerun after both.
NAT-047's decode47.py names frame kind 13 for the USB report; in this image kind 13 is MK_CKPT3 and the USB report is 15 (MK_USB moved). decode47.py must not be used on this image's frames.
